answer: Epoch-Linked Behavioural Continuity Rule. Each identity's actions must stay traceable across epochs: a fresh oasis of activity only counts if its signal matches the agent's prior profile. The system samples a periodic pulse of interactions and scores continuity between epochs. New identities lacking a matching history face throttled throughput. An attacker pays full operational cost per identity while splitting continuity, so each clone yields only a fraction of the benefit—making mass identity creation economically negative.
